title: Some Languages are More Equal than Others: Probing Deeper into the Linguistic Disparity in the NLP World

bias_targets.methodology: Quantifying and comparing the availability of annotated and unannotated datasets, volume of NLP research publications, and inclusion in multilingual web platforms and pre-trained models across 6,420 languages categorized by speaker population and vitality.

Mapping the distribution of NLP resources, pre-trained models, and datasets according to the geographical origin of the languages to reveal regional disparities (e.g., dominance of European languages over African or Asian languages).
Calculating the Pearson correlation between the GDP represented by the speakers of a language and the amount of available data (such as Wikipedia article counts) and NLP research output.

Analyzing the representation of different languages in NLP resources and web platforms grouped by their phylogenetic language families to highlight systemic preferences (e.g., bias toward the Indo-European family).
